identification.summary: Storm-2035 is the Microsoft designation for an Iran-linked network that ran websites posing as local US news outlets and posted divisive content aimed at both Democratic and Republican audiences [S1][S2][S6]. Microsoft described it in August 2024 as separate from the IRGC-linked cyber actors (Mint Sandstorm, Peach Sandstorm) named in the same reporting [S1][S6]. OpenAI later banned ChatGPT accounts it tied to Storm-2035 that were generating articles and social media comments [S3][S4]. A later Meta report attributed a separate cluster to Storm-2035 [S7].
identification.firstObserved: Publicly described by Microsoft in August 2024 [S1][S6]. Earlier activity dates are not stated in the sources gathered.
identification.notes: Named sites in press coverage of Microsoft's report include EvenPolitics, Savannah Time and Nio Thinker (four sites in total) [S2][S6]. Microsoft's separate cyber-enabled influence actor Cotton Sandstorm (Emennet Pasargad) is a different Microsoft cluster and is not merged here [S8]. This is an influence-operation designation, not an intrusion set.

attribution.sponsor: Microsoft describes Storm-2035 as Iranian [S1][S2]. A specific Iranian government organization is not named in the sources gathered.
attribution.confidence: Confidence level is not stated in the secondary coverage reviewed. Iran's UN mission denied interfering in the US election [S1][S6].
attribution.basis: Microsoft Threat Analysis Center reporting (read via secondary coverage) [S1][S2][S6]; OpenAI account-level findings [S3][S4]; Meta cluster attribution to Storm-2035 [S7].

objectives: Inflame partisan tensions in the US by engaging voter groups at both ends of the political spectrum with polarizing messaging on the presidential candidates, LGBTQ rights and the Israel-Hamas conflict [S1][S2][S3].

sectors: US voters and political audiences (Democratic- and Republican-leaning)
regions: Azeri-speaking audiences in Azerbaijan and Turkey (Meta cluster attributed to Storm-2035, per secondary coverage) [S7]
targeting.notes: Sites were tailored by audience, for example Nio Thinker aimed at liberal readers and Savannah Time presented as conservative [S2][S5]. OpenAI saw content in English and Spanish [S3][S4].

capabilities.summary: Fake local-news websites posting politically divisive content [S1][S2]. Use of ChatGPT to write long-form articles and short social media comments, posted by more than a dozen personas on X and one on Instagram, with articles on five websites [S3][S4]. OpenAI assessed the operation did not gain meaningful audience engagement; most posts received few or no likes, shares or comments [S3][S5]. Meta tied the Instagram account to an Iranian network it disrupted in December 2022 [S3][S5].

campaigns.name: Microsoft discloses fake US news site network
campaigns.summary: Microsoft Threat Analysis Center reported Storm-2035 running four websites posing as news outlets with divisive content targeting both US political camps, in a report that also covered IRGC-linked Mint Sandstorm and Peach Sandstorm [S1][S2][S6].

campaigns.name: OpenAI bans ChatGPT accounts
campaigns.summary: OpenAI banned accounts used to generate long-form articles and social media comments in English and Spanish for Storm-2035; it found little audience engagement [S3][S4][S5].

campaigns.name: OpenAI links an account to IUVM and Storm-2035
campaigns.summary: Per search-result summary of an OpenAI report (not opened), one banned account generated content for both IUVM and Storm-2035, suggesting an operator-level relationship [S9].

campaigns.name: Meta Q1 2025 disruption
campaigns.summary: Meta's Q1 2025 adversarial threat report disrupted an Iranian network attributed to the Storm-2035 cluster, reported as targeting Azeri-speaking audiences with fake personas across Facebook, Instagram and other sites [S7].

diamond.adversary: Iran-linked influence network designated Storm-2035; specific sponsor unnamed in gathered sources [S1][S2].
diamond.capability: Fake news sites, fake personas on X and Instagram, AI-generated text [S1][S3][S4].
diamond.infrastructure: Websites such as EvenPolitics, Savannah Time and Nio Thinker; social accounts on X and Instagram [S2][S3][S6]. Hosting details are not in the sources gathered.
diamond.victim: US voters of both political leanings [S1][S2]; Azeri-speaking audiences in a Meta-attributed cluster [S7].
diamond.socioPolitical: Exploiting US election-season polarization and issues such as the Israel-Hamas conflict and LGBTQ rights [S1][S2].
diamond.technology: Social media platforms, web publishing and a commercial generative-AI service whose providers could detect and ban accounts [S3][S4].

gaps: Microsoft's original August 2024 report could not be fetched (host unreachable); details rely on secondary coverage [S1][S2][S6].
OpenAI's own case study (dated 2024-10-01 per search summary) and its Feb 2025 report could not be opened; the IUVM link rests on a search summary [S5][S9].
Sponsoring Iranian organization, confidence level and actor-to-state tasking are not stated in gathered sources.

Whether the Meta Storm-2035 cluster (Azeri-speaking targeting) is the same operators as the 2024 US-focused network is unverified; Meta's report was not opened and the Hacker News summary is ambiguous on targeting [S7].
Relationship to Cotton Sandstorm/Emennet Pasargad is not established; Microsoft reports them as separate [S8].
No post-2025 activity found; a Scotland-related claim could not be verified and is excluded.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: The operational environment is the US information environment, including news-like websites and social platforms. STEP 2: The network used low-cost tools with limited engagement, so impact on audiences was low [S3][S5]. STEP 3: Template is fake local-news sites, personas on X and Instagram, and AI-generated English and Spanish text [S2][S3]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued polarizing content aimed at US audiences around elections and the Israel-Hamas conflict [S1]. MDCOA is better-concealed, more tailored personas or amplification by other Iranian actors that gain traction. Candidate indicators: new local-news-style sites with unclear ownership, repeated persona accounts posting near-identical text, and takedown notices from platforms or AI providers [S3][S7].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track platform and AI-provider disclosures (Microsoft, OpenAI, Meta) as the main source of detection [S1][S3][S7]. (2) Authorities: influence operations against US audiences are outside most DoD network-defense authorities; route findings to appropriate interagency partners. (3) Mission assurance: personnel should be aware that fake news sites may target service members as voters. (4) Coordination: keep this cluster separate from IRGC cyber actors in reporting [S1][S6].
